#1347 Manual task-run worktree recycle — three root causes + fix tier=warm conf=0.95 lesson= when= eff_conf=1.00 sources=GoPi epic t-1788397248,commit 319f063 tokens=1 fb=0.75(2)
Q: Why did a manual gopi task run leave its worktree behind (and how was it fixed)? What were the three root causes?
A: Root cause of 'manual gopi task run leaves its worktree behind' (epic t-1788397248) and the fix, for reuse: (1) The finish-cleanup chain TaskFinishCleanupSessionID was client-gated — `if IsServerNode() { skip }` returned before ANY worktree removal, so server/single-node (zbook has no sync_peers) NEVER recycled. Fix: mode-split — IsServerNode() OR finishCleanupServerTarget()=="" (no peers) → new finishCleanupServerRecycle (worktree remove only, KEEP branch = merger input); client-with-peer → the existing push→remove→-d chain unchanged. (2) git worktree list --porcelain is MULTI-LINE — the chain's finishCleanupGit first-line summarizer truncated it, so the porcelain parsers (finishCleanupBranchWorktree, finishCleanupOwningWorktree) silently never matched a linked worktree. Fix: finishCleanupGitRaw raw-output reader; also the FIRST porcelain entry is the main checkout — never return it (skip on first). (3) The child's own end-hook chain runs on its AUTO row (no deliverable → skip); the WRAPPER row carries deliverable{repo,branch} but was closed by writeback with no chain call. Fix: delivery-time hook in runTaskRunOnce after completed writeback + mirror reconcile — the shared funnel for manual task run / task run next / worker round, so all recycle at delivery. Server arm guards: exempt branch (master etc), clean worktree (git status --porcelain — dirty = live bond skip), linked-worktree-on-branch resolution. File: internal/tools/task_finish_cleanup.go; devdoc/manual-taskrun-recycle-20260903.md.

#224 CivRealm evidence: LLM agents vs heuristic AI in turn-based 4X games tier=warm conf=0.85 lesson= when= eff_conf=1.00 sources=arXiv:2401.10568 (CivRealm); arXiv:2305.16291 (Voyager); arXiv:2303.11366 (Reflexion) tokens=1
Q: How well do LLM agents (GPT-4) perform playing Civilization VI via a text interface, and what are their failure modes?
A: CivRealm (Meta FAIR, arXiv:2401.10568) built a text-based interface to Civilization VI and evaluated GPT-4 / ReAct-style agents against the game's heuristic AI. Results: LLM agents LOST DECISIVELY (often 2-3x score gap) despite perfect symbolic state. Three failure modes, in order: (1) long-term planning / temporal credit assignment — agent abandoned its own 50-turn-old goals because each prompt was fresh context; (2) resource/economy management — spammed unpayable units, misordered build queues, settled cities on bad tiles; (3) spatial reasoning — textual grid caused circular movement, ignored river defense bonuses, failed adjacency rules. Transferable lesson for any LLM-in-4X project (HoMM3/VCMI included): the bottleneck is cognition not perception; mitigate with persistent plan memory + reflection (Reflexion), skill libraries (Voyager), and engine-computed tools for pathfinding/danger instead of raw grids. Also: a non-vision LLM CAN drive a GUI 4X game through a text bridge — the modality is not the blocker.

keywords: CivRealm Civ VI LLM agent benchmark, GPT-4 lose strategy game heuristic AI, LLM 4X game failure long-term planning spatial, text interface turn-based strategy LLM, Voyager skill library Reflexion reflection game, LLM agent cognition not perception bottleneck
